clue.text: Public officer

explanation.definitionFit: General means common or public, as in the general good, and a general is a senior army officer.

clue.text: Warmer, like the man in great shape

indicators.note: in says the short pieces go inside the reworked letters
shape says the word great is put into a new form

parts.note: as means like, as in proud as a peacock
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A heater compared to a man who is very fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: an appliance. 'in great shape' reads as fitness, while 'shape' rearranges and 'in' contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas heater is a domestic appliance that warms a room.

clue.text: Inadequate, as is well known

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means not capable, and as one word it means famous or prominent.

clue.text: Conscience-stricken about jailed social worker

parts.note: re means about, concerning
pent means shut up or confined
an ant is a social insect that works for its colony

explanation.surface: A social worker who has been locked up is full of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a job, but the ant is a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A repentant person regrets wrongdoing and feels remorse.

clue.text: Left work on early side to run

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
E is east, the side where the day begins earliest

explanation.surface: Someone who quit work to go jogging in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to move with long easy strides, a relaxed running gait.

clue.text: One of the family assuming a right which is questionable

parts.note: an uncle is a relative, a member of the family

explanation.surface: A relative who takes up some right of dubious standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assuming' just joins the pieces: UNCLE takes on A and R after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is doubtful or open to question.

clue.text: Tear into a French head showing a lack of maturity

indicators.note: into says the tear word goes inside the French article

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a
to rip is to tear
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Ripping into a French boss reveals immaturity.
explanation.definitionFit: Unripeness is the state of not being fully developed, like fruit not yet ready.

clue.text: Jewish name for firm poultry

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a hen is a domestic fowl

explanation.surface: A Jewish surname belonging to a chicken company.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohen is a common Jewish surname, traditionally borne by the priestly line.

clue.text: Farm animal we blame for damage

indicators.note: damage says these letters are broken up and put together differently

explanation.surface: A farmer blames a beast for the harm done.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young female sheep, a farm animal.

clue.text: Get stormed at, being in debt

annotationWithheld.why: Get stormed at, being in debt (5): the only parse is AT inside RED for RATED with 'at' also in the definition 'stormed at', so 'at' does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Get stormed at, being in debt

clue.text: Drink around it — don't go to bed

indicators.note: around says the drink word is wrapped about the next piece

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone nursing a drink late into the night instead of going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit up is to stay awake past bedtime rather than retire for the night.

clue.text: Stiff paper for leading soldiers during exercises

indicators.note: during says the soldiers' letters sit inside the exercises abbreviation

parts.note: PT stands for physical training, school exercises
arch as an adjective means chief or leading, as in arch-enemy
men is the usual crossword word for soldiers or other ranks

explanation.surface: Stiff paper set aside for senior officers taking part in manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is a heavy, stiff writing material, originally prepared animal skin.

clue.text: Falling in the main

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea, and falling there describes a tide going out

explanation.surface: Something mostly or chiefly in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but here the main is the ocean, whose tide falls as it retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide that recedes from the shore is said to be on the way out, sinking back from high water.

clue.text: Endless praise and build-up for a European

indicators.note: build-up says the letters are put together afresh in a new order
endless says the word praise loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Unending praise and hype aimed at someone from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts PRAISE to PRAIS; 'build-up' rearranges PRAIS with AND into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Spain is a European.

clue.text: Pedantic but chic, as lots may be

indicators.note: may be says the letters of these words could be arranged as something else

explanation.surface: Someone fussy yet stylish, as a lot of people can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholastic can mean pedantic, from the hair-splitting of medieval schoolmen.

clue.text: Some loathe taking a letter

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people hate accepting a piece of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: He painted pictures — many on racehorses

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
taken as written
a stable is a group of racehorses kept by one trainer

explanation.surface: An artist who painted lots of pictures of horses at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape painter, so he is someone who painted pictures.

clue.text: Restrained irritation over a note

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: temper is a fit of anger or irritation
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Controlled annoyance about a short message.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and self-controlled.

clue.text: Military command looks good

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at
right means correct or good

explanation.surface: An order on the parade ground looks fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is a parade-ground order to turn the head to the right in salute.

clue.text: Rough site being transformed? That's good!

indicators.note: being transformed says the letters of these words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough patch of land is being improved, and that's a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright, virtuous.

clue.text: The bride must be soigne

explanation.definitionFit: A bride needs a bridegroom, so she must be supplied with one; separately the word means well turned out and sleek.

clue.text: It's extra to include second means of communication

indicators.note: to include says the extra word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: more means additional or extra
S is the abbreviation for second, the unit of time

explanation.surface: An additional message channel is thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse code sends letters as dots and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code is a signalling system of dots and dashes used for telegraph messages.

clue.text: Rebuke salesman on promenade

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
to promenade is to stroll, to wander or rove

explanation.surface: Telling off a salesman on the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promenade' looks like a seafront walkway, but here it is a verb, to stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to scold or criticise.

clue.text: Liberal all for a student accepting work on the land

indicators.note: accepting says the first group of pieces takes the work word inside it

parts.note: being all for something is being pro it
L is the learner plate, a student driver
to dig is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician, fully behind a student taking up farm work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital looks political, but here it means lavish or free-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means generous to the point of extravagance, freely giving.

clue.text: Over a quarter will get a spread

parts.note: past means over, finished
E is east, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: More than a quarter of the money will buy something to put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste such as fish paste is a spread for bread.

clue.text: The whole Arab world is going on strike

indicators.note: going on says the next piece follows after the first

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: An entire region is downing tools in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but LAM means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam can mean the whole Muslim world, of which the Arab nations form the heartland.

clue.text: Shower season

explanation.definitionFit: To shower someone with shot or questions is to pepper them, and to season food can be to add pepper.

clue.text: A biscuit for the break

explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp biscuit, and to snap is to break suddenly.

clue.text: One's retiring representative revealed as a complete fool

indicators.note: retiring says the short possessive is read going backwards

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I plus S
MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
to let on is to reveal or disclose

explanation.surface: A shy MP is exposed as an utter idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like a shy personality trait of the representative, but it turns the possessive round.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: A wish to be in company

parts.note: to long for something is to wish for it

explanation.surface: Wanting to be part of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with someone means to accompany them, being together.

clue.text: Finish up with mice possibly becoming prevalent in the area

parts.note: to end up is to finish

indicators.note: possibly says the word mice may be arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: Mice end up becoming common throughout the district.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native to and common in a particular region.

clue.text: A gratuity for being in attendance

explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift or tip, and someone present is there in person rather than absent.
